Metadata.title: Technology Decisions for AgentMemBank MCP Server
Metadata.approval: Architecture approved by user before artifact generation; Agent UX + Admin Observability release approved 2026-05-10.

RuntimeStack.language: Python is the preferred runtime because MCP servers, async HTTP, SQLite tooling and filesystem safety are well-supported and easy to verify.
RuntimeStack.rationale: Python + asyncio keeps the server simple for local VPS deployment while supporting Streamable HTTP, file IO orchestration and testable service boundaries.

Transport.rationale: Private network transport reduces attack surface while allowing multiple MCP clients and agents to connect over HTTP.

Storage.rationale: Obsidian Sync may modify files outside the MCP server, therefore content-hash revision checks are required immediately before write.

DirectoryContractStack.optional_projection: AgentMemBank.md or configured system note in Vault, human-readable only
DirectoryContractStack.initial_semantic_keys: inbox memory summaries wiki log system
DirectoryContractStack.destination_resolution: Intent-inferred writes resolve through Directory Contract; generic capture falls back to canonical inbox; ambiguous structured writes require clarification.
DirectoryContractStack.alias_policy: Aliases are detected for drift and read compatibility, but deprecated aliases are denied as write targets by default.
DirectoryContractStack.obsidian_detection: Configured vault root should contain .obsidian unless explicitly disabled for tests.
DirectoryContractStack.rationale: A config-authoritative Directory Contract gives agents exact write destinations across all Vault folders while optional Markdown projection preserves Obsidian visibility without making service metadata the source of truth.

Database.writer_model: single_writer_queue (asyncio-based; all SQLite writes including index upserts, deletes and schema init must serialize through one writer to avoid SQLITE_BUSY under concurrent refresh)
Database.rationale: SQLite WAL and a single writer queue provide enough reliability for a personal Vault while avoiding external infrastructure.

SearchStack.rationale: FTS5 is reliable and rebuildable for MVP. sqlite-vec is preferred after MVP because it preserves local-first deployment; Qdrant remains optional for larger Vaults.

IndexSchema.rationale: The schema stores derivative metadata that can be rebuilt from Vault content and supports keyword, structural and future vector retrieval.

AuditStack.preferred_mvp: SQLite audit_log table (preferred for queryability and scalability). NDJSON append-only log is acceptable but must NOT use read-modify-write of entire file for each event — use append-only writes or rotating segments.
AuditStack.rationale: Machine-readable audit is necessary for traceability and verification; LOG.md is useful but not authoritative because Markdown can be manually edited or corrupted.

ProcessLoggingStack.storage: SQLite process_events table via IndexRepository or same database boundary
ProcessLoggingStack.event_categories: boot config auth mcp_request policy read mutation file_change promotion index_refresh sync_external_change backup membank_init vault_layout admin_dashboard error
ProcessLoggingStack.filter_fields: from_timestamp to_timestamp severity category event_type agent_id admin_user path_prefix trace_id status error_code
ProcessLoggingStack.redaction: No API keys, admin passwords, Authorization headers, raw note content, raw patch body or denylisted content in process events, dashboard or reports.
ProcessLoggingStack.rationale: SQLite-backed process events support filtering and timeline reconstruction, while .log export gives portable debug artifacts without exposing raw Vault content.

SecurityStack.auth_model: API key to agent identity and policy profile

profiles.profile: trusted operations except delete and bulk move

SecurityStack.rationale: Profiles limit blast radius when an agent is compromised or issues an incorrect tool call.

AdminDashboardStack.web_runtime: aiohttp routes co-hosted or mounted beside Streamable HTTP transport
AdminDashboardStack.admin_auth: separate login/password session auth; credentials loaded from env/config as hash or secret reference
AdminDashboardStack.release_scope: read-only debug dashboard: status, event filters, errors, file changes, MCP requests and .log export
AdminDashboardStack.forbidden_scope: No Vault editing, delete, rollback or destructive admin controls in this release
AdminDashboardStack.rationale: Admin UI improves operability but must not expand mutation surface; separating dashboard auth from MCP API-key auth keeps human and agent trust domains distinct.

ObservabilityStack.durable_process_events: required for admin dashboard and report export
ObservabilityStack.trace_correlation: trace_id must correlate structured logs, process events, audit records and .log report lines
ObservabilityStack.rationale: Autonomous agents need precise trace evidence for policy decisions, patch validation, lock acquisition, revision checks, audit and index refresh.

TestingStack.sqlite_tests: temporary SQLite databases with WAL checks
TestingStack.contract_tests: MCP tool contract tests and policy matrix tests
TestingStack.trace_tests: log/trace anchor assertions for critical flows
TestingStack.rationale: Tests must verify contracts, not just implementation details, because autonomous execution depends on stable module boundaries.

DiscouragedTechnologies.technology: Public internet exposure for MCP endpoint
Free-form regex patch as default edit mechanism
Delete and bulk move operations in MVP
Agent-inferred folder creation outside Directory Contract
Admin dashboard sharing MCP API-key auth as web login
Plaintext admin passwords in config or logs
Raw note content or raw patch bodies in debug logs
DiscouragedTechnologies.rationale: These choices weaken safety, verification, recoverability or local-first deployment.
